headline: Two DGFI members dismissed and jailed for a year in extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were sentenced following a court martial after attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.
The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested on October 25 after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.
The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.
Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to purchase a motorcycle, but four people entered and confined him, demanding the money.
The victim also handed over Tk 70,000 he had brought for the purchase before being assaulted and threatened again.
Around 3:00 am on October 25, Sharif was forced into a car and taken out of the flat. He managed to escape and inform a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli.
Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car. The two personnel were later handed over to the army for trial under military law.
Intelligence sources confirmed that the allegations against the two were proved during the court martial proceedings, leading to their dismissal and sentencing.
caption:
Two DGFI members have been dismissed and sentenced to one year in prison for attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.

Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.

The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested on October 25 after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.

The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.

Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to purchase a motorcycle, but four people entered and confined him, demanding the money.

The victim also handed over Tk 70,000 he had brought for the purchase before being assaulted and threatened again.

Around 3:00 am on October 25, Sharif was forced into a car and taken out of the flat. He managed to escape and inform a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli.

Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car. The two personnel were later handed over to the army for trial under military law.

Intelligence sources confirmed that the allegations against the two were proved during the court martial proceedings, leading to their dismissal and sentencing.

headline_marked: Ibrahim's super-sub goal: [[Bangladesh beat Bhutan 1-0]] in SAFF opener
headline: Ibrahim's super-sub goal: Bangladesh beat Bhutan 1-0 in SAFF opener
summary: Mohammad Ibrahim scored the winning goal just four minutes after coming off the bench to secure a victory for Bangladesh.
details: Bangladesh secured a 1-0 victory over Bhutan in their SAFF Championship opening match at the National Stadium on Thursday.
Forward Mohammad Ibrahim provided the instant impact, scoring the decisive goal in the 69th minute after entering the game in the 65th minute.
Head coach Thomas Dooley admitted he was surprised by the goal, stating he brought Ibrahim on primarily to hold the ball and set up other players.
The match featured an unusual tactical move by Dooley, who initially deployed centre-back Bishwanath Ghosh as a lone striker.
Dooley praised Bishwanath's energy and work rate up front, noting that the defender's power made him difficult for opponents to defend against.
Ibrahim's goal comes as a reward for his recent strong form, having recently scored a crucial goal for Fortis FC in the AFC Challenge League.
Bangladesh is now looking to reclaim the SAFF title, which they last won in 2003.
caption:
A super-sub impact! Mohammad Ibrahim scores just 4 minutes after coming on to lead Bangladesh to victory.

Bangladesh secured a 1-0 victory over Bhutan in their SAFF Championship opening match at the National Stadium on Thursday.

Forward Mohammad Ibrahim provided the instant impact, scoring the decisive goal in the 69th minute after entering the game in the 65th minute.

Head coach Thomas Dooley admitted he was surprised by the goal, stating he brought Ibrahim on primarily to hold the ball and set up other players.

The match featured an unusual tactical move by Dooley, who initially deployed centre-back Bishwanath Ghosh as a lone striker.

Dooley praised Bishwanath's energy and work rate up front, noting that the defender's power made him difficult for opponents to defend against.

Ibrahim's goal comes as a reward for his recent strong form, having recently scored a crucial goal for Fortis FC in the AFC Challenge League.

Bangladesh is now looking to reclaim the SAFF title, which they last won in 2003.
